summary: Franklin County, VA Cahas Mountain tower, removed circa 2007-2008 after vandalism; register says The Nature Conservancy owns the site, and a conservation group describes it differently.

facts.status_note: Tower removed circa 2007-2008; no source describes what, if anything, remains on the site

access.note: Register says The Nature Conservancy owns the site now; a Blue Ridge Land Conservancy hike notice says the view from the top is on private land it conserves, and names no owner. The Cahas hike is guided, ticketed and limited to 15. No public access described.

events.note: Register: removed circa 2007-2008 after repeated vandalism; the Franklin County forestry office decided on removal

evidence.supports: one of many towers protecting this section of southern Virginia
evidence.quote: The tower on Cahas Mountain was one of many towers protecting this section of southern Virginia.

evidence.supports: vandalism and county forestry office decision to remove
evidence.quote: This tower suffered many bouts of vandalism before the forestry office in Franklin County made the decision to remove it.
All of the Franklin County towers have been removed.

evidence.supports: The Nature Conservancy owns the site now
evidence.quote: The site is now owned by The Nature Conservancy.

evidence.supports: hike notice says the view from the top of Cahas Mountain is on private land the conservancy conserves
evidence.quote: You will enjoy a fabulous view on private land that is conserved by Blue Ridge Land Conservancy.

evidence.supports: hike to the top of Cahas Mountain
evidence.quote: hike to the top of Cahas Mountain

evidence.supports: Cahas Mountain is Franklin County's highest peak
evidence.quote: dominated by Cahas Mountain, Franklin County's highest peak

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says The Nature Conservancy owns the site; a Blue Ridge Land Conservancy hike notice says the view from the top of Cahas Mountain is on private land it conserves, and names no owner. Not resolved; the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: No build date, design or staffing in the sources read. The 1996 NRHP nomination PDF and the Franklin County communities PDF were checked and mention no tower. Removal date is only 'circa'. Ownership unresolved (register: TNC owns; BRLC notice: land it conserves, no owner named); check TNC or county records. Access is private; no tower to climb. Two web searches used.
